tools.paint-calculator.faqs.0.question: How much paint do I need for a 12x12 room?
tools.paint-calculator.faqs.0.answer: A 12x12 room with 8-foot ceilings has about 384 square feet of wall area. Subtract a door (about 21 sq ft) and a window (about 15 sq ft), and you have roughly 348 square feet of paintable surface. With 2 coats and standard coverage of 350 sq ft per gallon, you'll need about 2 gallons of paint.
tools.paint-calculator.faqs.1.question: How many square feet does a gallon of paint cover?
tools.paint-calculator.faqs.1.answer: A gallon of interior latex paint typically covers 350-400 square feet per coat on smooth surfaces. Textured walls, unpainted drywall, or porous surfaces can reduce coverage to 200-300 sq ft per gallon. Premium paints sometimes offer higher coverage, around 400+ sq ft per gallon.
tools.paint-calculator.faqs.2.question: Should I buy gallons or quarts of paint?
tools.paint-calculator.faqs.2.answer: Gallons are more cost-effective per unit volume. Quarts typically cost about 30% of the gallon price but only contain 25% of the paint. Buy gallons for large areas, and quarts only for small touch-ups or accent walls under 100 square feet. This calculator shows the best combination.
tools.paint-calculator.faqs.3.question: How do I calculate paint for a room with vaulted ceilings?
tools.paint-calculator.faqs.3.answer: For vaulted or cathedral ceilings, use this calculator's manual mode. Measure each wall separately, calculate the area of triangular or trapezoid walls (base * average height), then enter the total wall area. Remember to subtract doors and windows as usual.
tools.paint-calculator.faqs.4.question: Do I need to calculate primer separately?
tools.paint-calculator.faqs.4.answer: Yes. Primer coverage differs from paint, typically 200-300 square feet per gallon. If painting over dark colors, new drywall, or stained surfaces, add a primer coat before the paint coats. Some paint-and-primer combo products may skip this step, but separate primer works better on problem surfaces.
tools.paint-calculator.faqs.5.question: How much extra paint should I buy?
tools.paint-calculator.faqs.5.answer: Buy 10-15% extra paint to account for touch-ups, mistakes, and future repairs. This calculator rounds up to the nearest gallon, which usually provides that buffer. Store leftover paint sealed for future touch-ups, since exact color matching can be difficult later.
tools.paint-calculator.faqs.6.question: How do I estimate paint for textured walls?
tools.paint-calculator.faqs.6.answer: Textured walls absorb more paint. For light texture, reduce coverage to about 300 sq ft per gallon. For heavy texture like stucco or popcorn, use 200-250 sq ft per gallon. Adjust the coverage field in this calculator to match your wall texture for a more accurate estimate.
tools.paint-calculator.labels.error: Door and window area cannot be larger than wall area.
tools.paint-calculator.guide.whatIs.titl: How to Use the Paint Calculator
tools.paint-calculator.guide.whatIs.cont: Start by adding your rooms. For each room, enter the length, width, and ceiling height to automatically calculate the wall area, or switch to manual mode if you already know the total wall area. Add any doors and windows to subtract their area from the total. The calculator accounts for multiple coats and your paint coverage to give you the exact number of gallons.
tools.paint-calculator.guide.howTo.title: Paint Coverage by Type
tools.paint-calculator.guide.howTo.conte: Flat/Matte latex: 350-400 sq ft per gallon (ceilings, low-traffic rooms). Eggshell latex: 350-400 sq ft per gallon (living rooms, bedrooms). Satin latex: 350-400 sq ft per gallon (kitchens, bathrooms, hallways). Semi-gloss latex: 350-400 sq ft per gallon (trim, doors, cabinets). High gloss: 300-350 sq ft per gallon (trim, furniture, accents). Oil/Alkyd: 350-450 sq ft per gallon (trim, cabinets, high-wear areas). Primer (latex or shellac/oil): 200-300 sq ft per gallon (new drywall, stain blocking).
tools.paint-calculator.guide.tips.title: Surface Preparation Tips
tools.paint-calculator.guide.tips.conten: Before painting, clean the walls with a damp cloth or TSP solution to remove dust, grease, and dirt. Fill nail holes and cracks with lightweight spackle. Lightly sand glossy surfaces (120-150 grit) to help new paint adhere. Apply painter's tape to trim, ceiling edges, and any areas you want to protect. Use a stain-blocking primer on water stains, smoke damage, or when going from dark to light colors. Let the primer and each coat of paint dry completely (usually 2-4 hours for latex) before applying the next coat.

tools.payment-calculator.faqs.0.question: How do I calculate monthly payments?
tools.payment-calculator.faqs.0.answer: Monthly payments are calculated using the standard amortization formula: M = P[r(1+r)^n]/[(1+r)^n-1], where P is the loan amount, r is the monthly interest rate, and n is the total number of payments.
tools.payment-calculator.faqs.1.question: Does a longer term mean lower payments?
tools.payment-calculator.faqs.1.answer: Yes, longer terms have lower monthly payments, but you pay more total interest. A $25,000 loan at 6.5% has a $489 monthly payment over 5 years ($4,349 interest), versus $280 over 10 years ($8,580 interest).
tools.payment-calculator.faqs.2.question: What does this calculator not include?
tools.payment-calculator.faqs.2.answer: This only calculates principal and interest. Actual payments may include taxes, insurance, fees, and other escrow items depending on the loan type.

tools.profit-margin-calculator.faqs.0.qu: What is the difference between profit margin and markup?
tools.profit-margin-calculator.faqs.0.an: Profit margin is profit as a percentage of revenue (selling price). Markup is profit as a percentage of cost. $60 profit on $100 revenue is a 60% margin, but a 150% markup on a $40 cost.
tools.profit-margin-calculator.faqs.1.qu: How do I calculate profit margin?
tools.profit-margin-calculator.faqs.1.an: Margin = ((Revenue - Cost) / Revenue) * 100. For example, selling at $100 with a cost of $40: ((100-40)/100) * 100 = 60% margin.
tools.profit-margin-calculator.faqs.2.qu: What is a good profit margin?
tools.profit-margin-calculator.faqs.2.an: It varies by industry. Software: 70-90%. Retail: 2-5%. Restaurants: 3-9%. Services: 15-30%. Manufacturing: 5-10%. Compare with industry averages.

tools.roi-calculator.faqs.0.question: How do I calculate ROI?
tools.roi-calculator.faqs.0.answer: ROI = ((Final Value - Initial Investment) / Initial Investment) * 100. For example, investing $1,000 with a final value of $1,500: ROI = ((1,500 - 1,000) / 1,000) * 100 = 50%.
tools.roi-calculator.faqs.1.question: What is annualized ROI?
tools.roi-calculator.faqs.1.answer: Annualized ROI converts returns into a yearly equivalent so you can compare investments across different periods. Formula: annualized ROI = ((Final Value / Initial Value)^(1/Years) - 1) * 100.
tools.roi-calculator.faqs.2.question: What is the difference between ROI and CAGR?
tools.roi-calculator.faqs.2.answer: ROI measures the total return percentage without considering time. CAGR (Compound Annual Growth Rate) measures the annual equivalent growth rate. For multi-year investments, CAGR provides better comparability.

tools.sales-tax-calculator.faqs.0.questi: How do I calculate sales tax?
tools.sales-tax-calculator.faqs.0.answer: Sales tax = Price * (Tax Rate / 100). For example, a $50 item at 7% tax: sales tax = 50 * (7/100) = $3.50, total = 50 + 3.50 = $53.50.
tools.sales-tax-calculator.faqs.1.questi: How do I remove sales tax from a total?
tools.sales-tax-calculator.faqs.1.answer: Pre-tax price = Total / (1 + Tax Rate/100). If the total is $107 at 7% tax: pre-tax price = 107 / (1 + 7/100) = 107 / 1.07 = $100.
tools.sales-tax-calculator.faqs.2.questi: Which states have no sales tax?
tools.sales-tax-calculator.faqs.2.answer: Five states have no state sales tax: Alaska, Delaware, Montana, New Hampshire, and Oregon. Note that local jurisdictions may still impose their own sales taxes.

tools.simple-interest-calculator.metadat: Calculate simple interest and see the formula, with comparison to compound interest.
Simple interest is calculated only on the initial principal. Formula: Interest = Principal * Rate * Time. Unlike compound interest, your earnings don't generate earnings of their own.
What is the difference between simple and compound interest?

Simple interest is calculated only on the principal. Compound interest is calculated on the principal and accumulated interest. $1,000 at 5% for 3 years: simple interest = $150. Compound interest = $157.63. The difference grows with time and rate.
Simple interest is used for auto loans, personal loans, and short-term loans. Most mortgages and credit cards use compound interest. Always confirm which type your loan uses.
How do I calculate the amount due?
Amount Due = Principal + Interest. Or: Amount Due = Principal * (1 + Rate * Time). $1,000 at 5% for 3 years: amount due = 1,000 * (1 + 0.05 * 3) = $1,150.

tools.square-footage-calculator.faqs.0.q: How do I calculate the square footage of a room?
tools.square-footage-calculator.faqs.0.a: Measure the room's length and width in feet, then multiply them together. For example, a 12-foot by 10-foot room is 120 square feet. If the room is not a simple rectangle, break it into smaller rectangles, calculate each area, and add them together.
tools.square-footage-calculator.faqs.1.q: How many square feet are in an acre?
tools.square-footage-calculator.faqs.1.a: There are exactly 43,560 square feet in an acre. To convert square feet to acres, divide the square feet by 43,560. For example, 10,000 square feet is approximately 0.23 acres.
tools.square-footage-calculator.faqs.2.q: How do I convert square feet to square meters?
tools.square-footage-calculator.faqs.2.a: Multiply square feet by 0.0929 to get square meters. For example, 500 square feet is approximately 46.45 square meters. To convert from square meters to square feet, multiply by 10.764.
tools.square-footage-calculator.faqs.3.q: How do I calculate the square footage of an irregularly shaped room?
tools.square-footage-calculator.faqs.3.a: Break the irregular shape into standard geometric shapes such as rectangles, triangles, or circles. Calculate the area of each shape separately, then add them all together. This calculator's L-shaped mode and room calculator make common layouts simple.
tools.square-footage-calculator.faqs.4.q: How much flooring do I need? Should I buy extra?
tools.square-footage-calculator.faqs.4.a: Calculate the total square footage of all rooms to be floored. Standard practice is to add 10% extra material for waste from cuts, mistakes, and future repairs. For diagonal or pattern installations, add 15-20% extra material.
tools.square-footage-calculator.faqs.5.q: What is the difference between square feet and linear feet?
tools.square-footage-calculator.faqs.5.a: Linear feet measure length in a straight line (one dimension), while square feet measure area (two dimensions). For example, a board 1 foot wide and 8 feet long is 8 linear feet and also 8 square feet. Knowing the difference matters when buying materials.
tools.square-footage-calculator.guide.wh: How to Use the Square Footage Calculator

tools.tax-calculator.keywords.11: how much tax do i pay
tools.tax-calculator.faqs.0.question: What taxes does this calculator include?
tools.tax-calculator.faqs.0.answer: This calculator estimates four taxes: federal income tax (using 2026 brackets), Social Security tax (6.2%, up to $176,100), Medicare tax (1.45%, plus an extra 0.9% on income over $200,000), and state income tax. It does not include local taxes, self-employment tax, or capital gains tax.
tools.tax-calculator.faqs.1.question: Is this calculator accurate?
tools.tax-calculator.faqs.1.answer: This provides a reliable estimate for W-2 employees. Actual taxes depend on many factors, including tax credits (Child Tax Credit, Earned Income Tax Credit), additional income sources, and state-specific rules. Use it as a planning tool, not a substitute for filing.
tools.tax-calculator.faqs.2.question: Why is my effective rate lower than my bracket?
tools.tax-calculator.faqs.2.answer: Tax brackets are marginal - only the income within each bracket is taxed at that rate. If you earn $85,000 (single), your first $11,925 is taxed at 10%, the next portion at 12%, and so on. Your effective rate averages all brackets, so it is always lower than your highest marginal bracket.
tools.tax-calculator.faqs.3.question: Do 401(k) contributions reduce my taxes?
tools.tax-calculator.faqs.3.answer: Yes. Traditional 401(k) contributions are pre-tax, meaning they reduce your federal and state taxable income. Contributing $10,000 to a 401(k) while in the 22% bracket saves about $2,200 in federal tax alone. This calculator accounts for 401(k) and HSA contributions.
tools.tax-calculator.faqs.4.question: Which states have no income tax?
tools.tax-calculator.faqs.4.answer: Nine states have no income tax: Alaska, Florida, Nevada, New Hampshire, South Dakota, Tennessee, Texas, Washington, and Wyoming. However, these states typically make up the revenue through higher sales taxes, property taxes, or other fees.
tools.tax-calculator.faqs.5.question: What are FICA taxes?
tools.tax-calculator.faqs.5.answer: FICA stands for the Federal Insurance Contributions Act. It includes Social Security tax (6.2% on the first $176,100 of income) and Medicare tax (1.45% on all income, plus an additional 0.9% on income over $200,000). Your employer pays an equal amount.

tools.tdee-calculator.metadata.descripti: Calculate your Total Daily Energy Expenditure with multiple formulas, plus macronutrient split recommendations.
tools.tdee-calculator.faqs.0.question: What is TDEE?
tools.tdee-calculator.faqs.0.answer: Total Daily Energy Expenditure (TDEE) is the total number of calories you burn each day, including your Basal Metabolic Rate (BMR) plus all physical activity. Eating at your TDEE maintains your current weight.
tools.tdee-calculator.faqs.1.question: Which formula is most accurate?
tools.tdee-calculator.faqs.1.answer: Mifflin-St Jeor is considered the most accurate for most people. If you know your body fat percentage, Katch-McArdle is better because it accounts for lean body mass. Harris-Benedict is the oldest formula and tends to slightly overestimate.
tools.tdee-calculator.faqs.2.question: How do I lose weight using TDEE?
tools.tdee-calculator.faqs.2.answer: Subtracting 250-500 calories from your TDEE achieves steady weight loss of 0.5-1 pound per week. A 500-calorie daily deficit equals about 3,500 calories per week, roughly equal to 1 pound of fat.
tools.tdee-calculator.faqs.3.question: Why is activity level so important?
tools.tdee-calculator.faqs.3.answer: Activity level can change your TDEE by 40-60%. A sedentary person with a BMR of 1,700 has a TDEE of about 2,040, while a highly active person with the same BMR has a TDEE of about 2,930. Fill in your activity level honestly for accurate results.

tools.tile-calculator.metadata.title: Tile Calculator
tools.tile-calculator.metadata.descripti: Calculate the number of tiles needed based on area, tile size, and waste rate.
tools.tile-calculator.faqs.0.question: How do I calculate how many tiles I need?
tools.tile-calculator.faqs.0.answer: Measure the length and width of the area to get the total square footage. Divide it by the area of a single tile (in square feet) to get the base tile count. Then add 10-20% extra material for waste, cuts, and breakage based on your chosen layout pattern.
tools.tile-calculator.faqs.1.question: How much extra tile should I buy for waste?
tools.tile-calculator.faqs.1.answer: For standard straight/grid layouts, plan on 10% extra. Diagonal layouts typically need 15% waste, brick/offset patterns about 12%, and herringbone patterns about 20%. Complex room shapes with many cuts may need more. It's always better to have leftover tiles than to run out mid-project.
tools.tile-calculator.faqs.2.question: Does grout line size affect how many tiles I need?
tools.tile-calculator.faqs.2.answer: Yes. Wider grout lines slightly reduce the number of tiles needed because each tile actually covers a larger footprint (tile + half a grout line on each side). A standard 1/8-inch grout line has little effect, but larger 1/4-inch or 3/8-inch gaps can noticeably reduce tile count over large areas.
tools.tile-calculator.faqs.3.question: How do I convert tile size from inches to square feet?
tools.tile-calculator.faqs.3.answer: Multiply the tile width by the height (in inches) to get square inches, then divide by 144 (since 1 square foot = 144 square inches). For example, a 12x24-inch tile is 288 square inches / 144 = 2 square feet per tile.
tools.tile-calculator.faqs.4.question: What is the most cost-effective tile layout pattern?
tools.tile-calculator.faqs.4.answer: Straight or grid patterns are the most cost-effective because they produce the least waste (about 10%). Brick/offset adds about 12%, diagonal about 15%, and herringbone about 20%. The extra cost comes from more cuts and unusable remnants. Straight layouts also install faster, lowering labor costs.
tools.tile-calculator.faqs.5.question: How do I calculate tile for a wall or backsplash?
tools.tile-calculator.faqs.5.answer: Use the same method as for floors: measure the wall height and width to get the area, then subtract any windows, doors, or outlets. Enter these dimensions into the calculator and it will compute the tiles needed. For backsplashes, measure from the countertop to the bottom of the upper cabinets.
tools.tile-calculator.faqs.6.question: Should I round up tiles or boxes?
tools.tile-calculator.faqs.6.answer: Always round up. You can't buy partial tiles or partial boxes. This calculator automatically rounds up the number of tiles and boxes. Having a few extra tiles for future repairs is better than running out mid-installation.
tools.tile-calculator.guide.whatIs.title: How to Use the Tile Calculator
tools.tile-calculator.guide.whatIs.conte: This tile calculator helps you determine the exact number of tiles, boxes, and total cost needed for any tiling project. Whether you're tiling a bathroom floor, kitchen backsplash, or an entire room, follow these steps for an accurate estimate.
tools.tile-calculator.guide.howTo.title: Step-by-Step Instructions
tools.tile-calculator.guide.howTo.conten: Step 1: Enter your area dimensions - measure the length and width of the area you're tiling. You can enter measurements in feet and inches, or switch to metric for projects using meters. For irregularly shaped rooms, split the space into rectangles, calculate each one separately, then add the totals together. Step 2: Choose your tile size - select from common tile sizes like 12x12, 12x24, or 24x24 inches, or enter a custom tile size. The calculator accounts for grout line width when determining how many tiles fit in your space. Step 3: Choose a layout pattern - different layout patterns require different amounts of waste material due to cuts. Straight/grid is the most efficient, while herringbone requires the most extra material. The calculator automatically adjusts the waste percentage based on your chosen pattern, or you can set a custom waste percentage. Step 4: View results and cost - the results section shows the total number of tiles needed (with and without waste), the number of boxes to purchase, and the estimated total cost based on the price you entered.
tools.tile-calculator.guide.tips.title: Layout Patterns and Waste
tools.tile-calculator.guide.tips.content: Straight/Grid: about 10% waste (most efficient). Diagonal (45 degrees): about 15% waste. Herringbone: about 20% waste. Brick/Offset: about 12% waste. Complex room shapes with many cuts may need more. It's always better to have leftover tiles than to run out mid-project.
tools.net-worth-calculator.metadata.desc: Calculate net worth, tally assets and liabilities, including the debt-to-asset ratio.
tools.net-worth-calculator.faqs.0.answer: Net worth is what you own (assets) minus what you owe (liabilities). It measures financial health. A positive net worth means your assets exceed your debts. A negative net worth means your debts exceed your assets.
tools.net-worth-calculator.faqs.1.answer: Assets include: cash and savings accounts, investments (stocks, bonds, retirement accounts), real estate market value, vehicle value, personal property (jewelry, art), and retirement accounts.
tools.net-worth-calculator.faqs.2.answer: Liabilities include: mortgage balances, car loans, student loans, credit card debt, medical debt, personal loans, and any other money you owe.
tools.net-worth-calculator.faqs.3.questi: How often should I calculate my net worth?
tools.net-worth-calculator.faqs.3.answer: Track progress quarterly or semiannually. More frequent tracking can cause anxiety due to market fluctuations. An annual review is sufficient for long-term planning. The trend matters more than any single number.

Calculate your net worth by adding up assets and subtracting liabilities. Track your financial health.

tools.stock-profit-calculator.metadata.d: Calculate stock trading profit, rate of return, and break-even price, including commission fees.
tools.stock-profit-calculator.faqs.0.que: How do I calculate stock profit?
tools.stock-profit-calculator.faqs.0.ans: Profit = (Sell Price - Buy Price) × Shares - Commission. Include all fees paid when buying and selling. This gives your net profit, not just the price difference.
tools.stock-profit-calculator.faqs.1.que: How is the rate of return calculated?
tools.stock-profit-calculator.faqs.1.ans: Rate of return = (Profit ÷ Total Investment) × 100. Total investment = Buy Price × Shares + Buy Commission. This shows the percentage you earned, not just the dollar amount.
tools.stock-profit-calculator.faqs.2.que: Are dividends included in profit calculations?
tools.stock-profit-calculator.faqs.2.ans: Not by default, but they should be. Add any dividends received during the holding period to your sell proceeds. Total profit = capital gains + dividends - fees.
tools.stock-profit-calculator.faqs.3.que: How do taxes affect stock profits?
tools.stock-profit-calculator.faqs.3.ans: Short-term holdings (under one year) are taxed at ordinary income rates. Long-term holdings (over one year) are taxed at lower capital gains rates (0%, 15%, or 20%). Hold for more than a year to minimize taxes.

tools.credit-card-payoff-calculator.faqs: What happens if I only make minimum payments?

You pay the most interest and take the longest. On $10,000 at 18% APR with minimum payments (2% or $25): it takes over 30 years to pay off with more than $16,000 in interest. Always pay as much as you can.
What is the debt avalanche method?
The debt avalanche attacks the highest-rate card first while making minimum payments on the others. It mathematically saves the most interest and pays off debt the fastest.
What is a balance transfer card?
Balance transfer cards offer 0% APR for 12-18 months, typically charging a 3-5% fee. Savings are significant if you pay off the balance before the promo ends. If you don't, rates spike.
How do I stop adding to my credit card debt?

Remove saved card numbers. Use cash or debit. Build an emergency fund to cover unexpected expenses. Track spending to identify triggers. Address the root cause - insufficient income or excessive spending.

tools.down-payment-calculator.metadata.d: Calculate down payment amount and its impact on mortgage, monthly payment, and PMI.
tools.down-payment-calculator.faqs.0.que: How much should I put down?
tools.down-payment-calculator.faqs.0.ans: 20% for conventional loans to avoid PMI. FHA loans allow 3.5%, and VA loans require 0% (for eligible veterans). The lower your down payment, the higher your monthly payment and the more total interest you pay.
tools.down-payment-calculator.faqs.1.ans: Private mortgage insurance is required when your down payment is below 20%. It typically costs 0.3-1.5% of the loan amount per year. You can cancel PMI at 20% equity. Avoid it by putting down 20%.
tools.down-payment-calculator.faqs.2.que: How does the down payment affect interest rates?
tools.down-payment-calculator.faqs.2.ans: A larger down payment usually means a lower rate. A 20% down payment can save 0.25-0.5% compared to 5%. Lenders see more equity as lower risk. This reduces both your monthly payment and total interest.
tools.down-payment-calculator.faqs.3.que: Can I accept a gift as a down payment?
tools.down-payment-calculator.faqs.3.ans: Yes, from family members. Lenders require a gift letter and proof of funds. Some loans (investment properties) do not allow gifts. Document all sources.

tools.dividend-calculator.metadata.descr: Calculate dividend income, project growth with reinvestment and recurring contributions.
tools.dividend-calculator.faqs.0.answer: Dividend yield is the annual dividend per share divided by the stock price, expressed as a percentage. For example, a $50 stock paying a $2 annual dividend has a 4% yield (2 ÷ 50 × 100).
tools.dividend-calculator.faqs.1.answer: A DRIP (Dividend Reinvestment Plan) automatically uses your dividends to buy more shares, usually commission-free. This accelerates growth through compounding - your dividends buy more shares, which then generate more dividends.
tools.dividend-calculator.faqs.2.answer: Qualified dividends are taxed at the lower long-term capital gains rates (0%, 15%, or 20%). Non-qualified dividends are taxed at your ordinary income rate. The stock must be held for more than 60 days during the ex-dividend period to qualify for qualified treatment.
tools.dividend-calculator.faqs.3.questio: Is a higher dividend yield always better?
tools.dividend-calculator.faqs.3.answer: No. Unusually high yields (>8%) may signal a falling stock price or unsustainable dividends. Sustainable yields typically fall in the 2-6% range. Check the payout ratio - dividends paying out more than 60-70% of earnings may be at risk.
